title: Rabbi Yehoshua Unia or Uniya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is always mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud: at the end of Orlah 1:2 and the beginning of Shabbat 2:4, Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzchak says that Rabbi Yehoshua Unia taught. At the end of Shabbat 1:4, Rabbi Yehoshua Uniya teaches that the prohibition on “their daughters” means their eggs cooked by gentiles, not literal daughters, who are already forbidden by Torah law. It cites Rabbi Yishmael’s teaching: “Bat ha-yaanah”—the ostrich’s egg.
This shows that he was one of the teachers who recited baraitot.

notes.text: “Teachers who recited baraitot” does not by itself assign a Tannaitic historical generation. The egg interpretation is Hyman’s account of the cited teaching.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:4 directly names Yehoshua Onayya and the eggs/ostrich-egg interpretation. Hyman’s always statement and characterization as a reciter of baraitot are retained without assigning him a Tannaitic historical generation.
